children: The FTSE 100 credit-checking and consumer data group said the additional repurchase programme reflected the strength of its balance sheet and cash generation, with management confident in the outlook for the business.

For the six months ended 30 September, benchmark earnings advanced 15%, while revenue also increased, supported by broad-based growth across regions and business lines. North America remained the key driver, benefiting from demand for credit analytics, identity verification and fraud-prevention services.
Chief executive Brian Cassin said Experian delivered a strong first-half performance, highlighting continued momentum in both consumer services and business-to-business operations.

The company reiterated its medium-term growth ambitions and said it remained well positioned to benefit from structural trends including digitalisation, increasing regulatory requirements and rising demand for fraud and identity solutions.
Reporting by Frank Prenesti for Sharecast.com
